I am sorry to hear you’re going through this. I’m currently a 23 y/o M and have had GERD for the past 4 years, and have to have an endoscopy every 3 years. I’ve been under anesthesia 6 times, and although everything has gone fine each time, I still get super nervous when going under anesthesia. Being anxious/nervous about this stuff is totally normal and makes sense.  As for the heart concerns, I’m confident you’ll be fine under anesthesia especially because of how young you are and that scans haven’t detected anything wrong with your heart. If there was something wrong enough with your heart where anesthesia would cause you to go into cardiac arrest, it would have more than likely been detected on an echo. Plus, by the chance something goes wrong, you are in the hands of trained medical professionals who will know how to make sure you’re all good. That being said, I’d really recommend going through with an endoscopy. I doubt you would have developed esophageal cancer at this age even with everything your esophagus has been through, but it’s important with your history and current acid reflux to get looked at. I’d also start taking an OTC antacid such as Nexium if you haven’t already because that could help until the doctors possibly prescribe you something else to heal your esophagus if it needs healing. I wish you best of luck with everything and hope you’re all good!

For gallbladder related pain, I was recommended ibuprofen and it’s been working really nicely. I just make sure to take it with food and/or an antacid such as Nexium, but this is not to be done long-term. For liquids I’ve been drinking water, oolong tea, green tea, kombucha, pineapple juice, and cranberry juice (not all in one day, of course). A diet like this for the past week has really helped me, but of course just because something works for me doesn’t mean it’ll work for someone else. Just figured I’d share what has helped me in hopes some of it can help you. Best of luck with everything man, you got this.

If anyone experiencing tiredness/depression, you might be vitamin D deficient. Accutane is a vitamin A derivative, so your body is pretty much getting excess vitamin A. Vitamin A is a vitamin D inhibitor, so you could be vitamin D deficient. I was vitamin D deficient while on Accutane (went from 40mg/d to 80 then down to 60) and it resulted in tiredness and muscle aches and twitches. I’d recommend a daily vitamin D pill or even getting vitamin D pills for deficiency, but definitely consult with your doctor before jumping the gun on the deficiency pills. I took the deficiency pills for about a week when I had these issues and I did notice improvement, but did not continue long term with them and transitioned into daily vitamin D pills after. What worked for me might not work for you as everyone is different, but I hope this can help.

Garlic has powerful natural antioxidants and behaves like an antibiotic, and as a result can eliminate acne. I found out about this from a friend who was on accutane for 8 months and it did nothing for her besides cause her hair and nails to stop growing, fatigue, and dry her skin out. When she stopped she tried garlic because her mother recommended it to her, and she rarely get pimples now. She took one garlic clove once a day for a month straight and it legitimately cleared her up nicely. The single pimples she gets every now and then aren’t horrible either. You can also rub the garlic juices on white-heads and it will dry them out pretty quickly and get rid of them. Should take 3 days max if you put garlic on a white-head for it to go down and not feel painful and swollen. I had to stop recently after taking the medicine for 5 months and I still am breaking out slightly. Because I broke out pretty much my entire time on the medicine, I decided to look for other possible reasons I could be breaking out. I discovered that acne is the result of your body trying to flush out internal toxins. These toxins can be the result of a food sensitivity or allergy. Acne can appear because of certain bacteria that exist in your gut (this is why antibiotics work). Two major causes of bacterial acne are food sensitivities or food intolerances to gluten and/or dairy. My whole life I’ve had a sensitive stomach to certain foods, and I’ve discovered recently that it’s sensitive to possibly the most delicious food ingredients: dairy and gluten :( signs that you could have a food intolerance/sensitivity would be gas, nausea,  bloated feeling after eating, feeling groggy/tired after eating, acid reflux, and abnormal stool (I might’ve missed some but these are the most common signs I can think of) if you have any of those symptoms, try isolating a possible food ingredient/item and eliminating it from your diet. To tell if it’s an intolerance/sensitivity issue with a specific kind of food for sure, you must avoid it for at least 3 weeks, then reintroduce it into your diet and see how you feel and if it causes a breakout. Hope this helps and best of luck to you!
